title: Capabilities and Evaluation Biases of Large Language Models in Classical Chinese Poetry Generation: A Case Study on Tang Poetry

bias_targets.methodology: Constructing a 6x6 LLM-as-a-judge cross-evaluation matrix where models evaluate their own and peers' generated poetry to measure self-assessment inflation, peer-assessment convergence (echo chamber effects), and evaluator temperament (leniency vs. harshness), validated against human expert scores.

Using computational feature extraction and sentence embeddings to analyze semantic coherence and verify whether models accurately reproduce traditional Chinese imagery-emotion pairings (e.g., 'Willow' indicating 'Sadness'), thereby exposing cultural blind spots.
